title: The Gym to Fascism Pipeline
summary: A political-philosophical essay on why gym culture and young men lean right-wing: testosterone and self-selection, in-group/out-group dynamics, internal vs external locus of control, and the left's hostility to physicality. NH argues the left must embrace strength and aesthetics to win young lifters, and closes with his own creed that strength and kindness must go together.
claims: Most fitness influencers who look apolitical are, behind closed doors, conservatives or libertarians
A 2011 study linked low testosterone with progressive views and high testosterone with conservative views; raising T shifted only undecided men slightly rightward, and the sample was small
People self-select into activities matching their biology: aggressive, stress-tolerant, high-T men gravitate to combat sports and lifting
Lifting is a traditionally masculine pursuit whose in-group values (self-reliance, bootstraps) align with the right, and the online left became its out-group
Fitness is fixing yourself, which requires telling people what's wrong; an external locus of control is antithetical to self-improvement
The most motivating fitness icons, like David Goggins, embody an internal locus of control, even if not everyone can replicate their willpower
Many people use left-wing philosophy to rationalise a dislike of lifting, which is really an excuse to stay weak
Fit and unfit people talk past each other because of differing loci of control; 'just eat less' doesn't land with someone who feels powerless
A study found people with severe depression worsened faster when living with someone with a strong internal locus of control who blamed them
Societies with demanding standards produce excellence but also many failures; lower standards yield more success but more mediocrity
Fitness culture is elitist and aristocratic: if you make it you're good, if not nobody lowers the standards for you
Same water that softens the potato hardens the egg: some people thrive on negativity, others need positive reinforcement
Men gravitate toward the 'strong horse'; an ideology that promotes strength attracts young men regardless of its other content
Dismissing young men's perceived suffering only alienates them further; to replace a value you must offer a better one
The left should drop its hatred of physical culture; a Marxist with big arms and a big deadlift would be hugely popular with lifters
Gym culture isn't really fascist; it follows the aesthetics of fascism, including elitism, and edgy memes are youthful rebellion
He is fine with elitism: being fat, out of shape, smoking or doing drugs are bad and should be shunned, but compassion helps people overcome them
Anyone who lifts and wants to improve is his brother or sister regardless of background
Being kind without being strong is weakness, and being strong without being kind is useless; strength should help the weak
